extracted.intended_audience: utilities, attachers (broadband providers), and counsel/advisors working on pole-attachment matters
extracted.subtask_description: Clarifications and policy decisions in an FCC Declaratory Ruling and order addressing (inter alia) disclosure/transparency obligations, the meaning of “red tagged” and “necessitated solely,” cost-causation and cost-allocation for pole replacements, and certain procedural timelines and access rights for pole attachment applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loading studies — access and provision
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent pole inspection reports include loading studies, attachers will have access to such information under the new rule we adopt today; we will not, however, codify a requirement for a utility to provide an attacher with a loading study when it is not part of the inspection report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission declines to adopt a blanket rule requiring utilities to provide loading studies (as NCTA requested), but 'strongly encourage[s] utilities to provide such loading studies when reasonably requested and readily available.' The issue of cost recovery for loading studies is a separate cost issue not addressed here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age/height/class/condition and inspection dates disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Request to require utilities to provide data on the age, height, class, and condition of their poles, or the last date the pole was inspected, make-ready was conducted, or a pre-existing violation on the pole was fixed, is rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission finds attachers can often obtain this information through utilities during the application process or via their own pre-application surveys/inspections; to the extent such data are in pole inspection reports they are covered by the adopted transparency requirement and available upon request after an application is filed. The Commission 'strongly encourage[s] utilities to share this information when it is readily available and collected in the normal course of business.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of existing attachments and pending applications per pole
rubrics_metrics.description: Declines to require utilities to provide data on the number of attachments or pending attachment applications for each pole covered by an attachment request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: pole networks are dynamic, maintaining an up-to-date list would be time-consuming and expensive; potential benefits are outweighed by the burden. Even if some utilities track this, requiring universal compilation and ongoing updates would impose a considerable burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting data for make-ready estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: No new requirement adopted for utilities to provide more detailed supporting data in make-ready estimates; existing rules already require supporting cost details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existing rule: 47 CFR § 1.1411(d) requires supporting cost details in make-ready cost estimates. If utilities fail to comply, attachers may use the complaint process or mediation (see 47 CFR §§ 1.737, 1.1404 and FCC MDRD guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of financial records and continuing property records
rubrics_metrics.description: Declines to create new obligations requiring utilities to provide additional financial data regarding poles (including outside plant/continuing property records) as part of these rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission notes sections 1.1404(e) and (f) already require that 'pole owners, upon request of a cable operator or telecommunications carrier, provide the information they have relied on in calculating rates' and information an attacher seeks to rely on to show a rate is not just and reasonable. Because of existing rules and the focus on deployment rather than rate disputes, the Commission will not impose a broader duty to disclose additional financial records here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'red tagged' (clarified)
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of the Commission’s pole replacement policies, a 'red tagged' pole is one that the utility has identified as needing replacement for any reason other than the pole’s lack of capacity to accommodate a new attachment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission broadens prior usage (which required non-compliance with safety standards and placement on replacement schedule) to include any scenario where the utility identifies a pole for replacement for reasons other than lack of capacity. The Commission will not codify a single uniform label but clarifies how Commission use of 'red tagged' should be understood in the context of cost-allocation policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utilities' discretion regarding red-tagging and related labels
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission will not regulate utilities’ individual decisions regarding whether or how to 'red tag' poles; those decisions remain the sole responsibility of the utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the Commission clarifies its use of the term, it declines to formally codify a regulatory definition of 'red tagged' that prescribes how utilities must label poles. However, utilities may not evade cost-allocation rules by simply failing to 'red tag' a pole with safety violations or other preexisting conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Red tagging and cost allocation — prohibition on allocating all replacement costs to new attacher
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a pole is identified for replacement for reasons other than lack of capacity, a utility may not allocate all of the costs of that pole replacement to a new attacher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expanding 'red tag' prevents utilities from imposing 100% of pole-replacement costs on new attachers when replacement is required for non-capacity reasons; the Commission preserves utilities' right to deny attachment for lack of capacity but prevents misuse of red-tagging to shift unrelated replacement costs onto attachers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'necessitated solely' — illustrative examples
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission clarifies situations in which a pole replacement is not 'necessitated solely' by an attachment request because the pole already requires replacement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative (non‑exhaustive) examples where replacement is not 'necessitated solely' at the time of the attachment request: (1) replacement required pursuant to applicable law; (2) current pole fails applicable engineering standards (e.g., NESC); (3) utility’s previous or contemporaneous change to its internal construction standards necessitates replacement; (4) pole required to be replaced due to road expansion, property development, storm hardening, or similar government-imposed requirements; (5) pole already is on the utility’s internal replacement schedule (regardless of when scheduled). The Commission declines to codify a formal definition but provides these examples to aid application of cost-causation principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of §1.1408(b) cost-causation/cost-allocation to pole replacements
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost-allocation and cost-causation provisions in section 1.1408(b) apply to pole replacements: parties benefitting from a modification share proportionately in the costs, unless a modification is 'necessitated solely' by an additional or modified attachment of another party, in which case that party bears the costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applied to pole replacements, it is contrary to Commission rules and policies to require a new attacher to pay the entire cost of a pole replacement when the pole already requires replacement at the time the request is made. This application is grounded in precedent (including the Local Competition Order) and the Bureau's 2021 Pole Replacement Declaratory Ruling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utilities retain discretion to deny attachments for lack of capacity and to limit space‑saving techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilities retain the right to deny a new attachment request for a lack of capacity on a pole and have discretion to determine whether space-saving techniques (e.g., boxing, extension arms) are appropriate for a particular pole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission encourages utilities to allow attachers to use the same attachment techniques the utility itself uses in similar circumstances, but utilities may limit use where necessary to ensure safety, reliability, and sound engineering. The Commission declines to adopt a broad presumption that a pole should always be considered to have capacity where space-saving techniques exist; appropriateness is a utility determination under section 224(f)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples rejected as not germane to 'requires replacement' status
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission declines to include certain requested examples (e.g., pole unsalvageable for reuse, fully depreciated, or older than 30 years) as determinative of whether a pole must be replaced at the time a new attachment request is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission finds these examples are not germane to whether a pole must be replaced at the time of the attachment request and that including them would cause confusion or conflict with the overarching standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing timeline for first 3,000 poles
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarification that the first 3,000 poles in an attachment application are subject to the processing timeline set forth in section 1.1411(g)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit clarification resolving controversies about applicability of the processing timeline to large applications; parties should apply the timelines in 1.1411(g)(3) accordingly for the first 3,000 poles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachers' right to access documentation regarding utility easements
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarification of attachers' right to access documentation regarding utility easements is provided in the Declaratory Ruling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As part of the set of clarifications in the Declaratory Ruling, the Commission affirms attachers' rights to access easement documentation relevant to attachment requests; specifics are provided elsewhere in the order and are aimed at resolving disputes about evidentiary access during application and negotiation stages.
